messages:
maya: quick RFC follow-up idea: instead of a global safety budget, what about a tiny per-request 'fallback credit' that decays and refills? keeps decisions local but bounded.
li: short: how does this differ from the safety_budget proposal?
maya: safety_budget is long-lived per-tenant state. fallback-credit is ephemeral per-request or per-connection token we consume to allow a single low-bit fallback. credit is cheap to check and expires quickly so we avoid long-term drift.
zach: perf Q: per-request state sounds heavy. how to keep cheap?
maya: implement as a 16-bit atomic counter per-connection slot or per-worker+tenant fast table. runtime precomputes credit_cost per-mode (fp8=1, int8=3, 4bit=6). check is a single atomic_read and maybe an atomic_sub if choose low-bit. no allocations.
ron: how do credits refill? policy? can a noisy client drain credits and affect others?
maya: refill policies are configurable: periodic refill per-tenant, refill-on-idle, or token-burst at connection start. defaults: per-tenant refill window 60s and per-connection burst of N credits. noisy tenants get capped by per-worker tenant caps and eviction events emitted.
li: operator needs observability. what do we emit?
maya: emit credit_used events (sampled), credit_remaining_pct per-tenant per-minute, chosen_fallback, reason_code (CREDIT_OK / CREDIT_EXHAUST / METRIC_FAIL), envelope_version. dashboard panel for credit_exhaust_rate.
zach: router interaction: if credit_exhaust, do we auto-step to next fallback or fail the request?
maya: policy-driven: default is step to next higher fidelity. customers can opt for strict mode that returns 429 or queue. define in profile: on_credit_exhaust: fallback | queue | fail.
ron: audit & RBAC: who can enable aggressive refill?
maya: only platform+SRE can set global aggressive refill. tenant-level requests must include approver_id and justification in override metadata. all changes logged.
li: any hysteresis to avoid thrashing between modes?
maya: yes: per-connection cooldown window + per-tenant hysteresis thresholds (up_pct/down_pct) in envelope. runtime records last_transition_ts and enforces cooldown.
maya: actions: maya: write tiny schema + examples (48h). zach: microbench atomic credit ops and per-worker memory footprint (72h). ron: draft RBAC & dashboard alerts (48h). li: add credit metrics to observability schema (24h). ops-bot: created issue 9910: "fallback-credit: implement atomic credits + control-plane knobs"
li: small note: keep the fallback-credit additive, not replacement of envelope. envelope still governs quality thresholds.
maya: agreed. fallback-credit is a lightweight supplementary mechanism to give runtime safe flexibility. thanks :rocket:
